question: What is JCSV3?
answer: Jockey Club Student Village III (JCSV III) is a student residential village at The University of Hong Kong, located on Lung Wah Street, Kennedy Town [1]. It was named after The Hong Kong Jockey Club in recognition of a donation of HK$108.25 million from the Club’s Charities Trust [1]. The village consists of four Residential Colleges and is home to 1,800 students from 56 countries [1]. Its aim is to support students’ intellectual, social and cultural growth, and to foster cross-cultural experiences and lifelong friendships [1].

sources.title: Jockey Club Student Village III – The University of Hong Kong
sources.text:
Jockey Club Student Village III
Residential Colleges form part of a proud tradition at The University of Hong Kong.
Sited on Lung Wah Street, Kennedy Town, the Village was named after The Hong Kong Jockey Club in recognition of a donation of HK$108.25 million from the Club’s Charities Trust. Its four Residential Colleges are now home to 1,800 students, and are committed to contributing to society both locally and worldwide.
Each College is a home for students’ intellectual development as well as their social and cultural growth. In this community of young intellectuals, students learn about the world, about others, and most of all about themselves.
At The Jockey Club Student Village III, 1,800 students from 56 countries live together and learn from one another. Here, dynamic cross-cultural experiences take place, visions and ideals are nurtured, and friendships are built for life.

question: How do I book a room?
answer: Do you mean applying for a residential room, or booking a function/meeting room for an activity? The procedures are different.

question: How do I book a function room?
answer:
To book a function room, you should contact your floor tutor or tutor at least 3 working days before your desired time slot [1]. After booking, you will need to present the booking record (such as a calendar screenshot provided by your floor tutor) at the 4/F security counter to obtain a white access card for function rooms like A-301 [1][2]. If the security guard cannot recognize your booking, please contact the tutor who made the booking for you [1].

For all team and club events that involve using college technology (e.g., TV, projector, wireless microphones), you must test the equipment 2 days in advance [1]. If you encounter technical issues, report them to the tutor in charge of the event or team, as no last-minute on-site assistance will be provided [1].

question: What are the rules for overnight guests? Do any exceptions apply?
answer:
Overnight guests are not permitted at Jockey Club Student Village III. Guestrooms are not available in the Student Village, and visitors are not allowed to stay overnight [1]. Under the village Management Rules, visitors may visit between 09:00 and 23:00, with no entrance allowed after 22:30, and any visitor who stays after 00:00 is regarded as staying overnight and is subject to fines and disciplinary action [4]. The resident host must accompany the visitor, leave their Student Card at the security counter during the visit, and is responsible for the visitor’s conduct and any charges incurred [4].

At the general university level, the Regulations Governing Residential Colleges permit a visitor to stay overnight only in exceptional circumstances, with prior permission of the Master or duty tutor and payment of a prescribed charge [2][3]. However, because the JCSV III village rules explicitly prohibit overnight visitors, this general exception does not appear to be available in practice at the Student Village. Confirmation should be sought from the college or village office before relying on any exception.

question: What facilities are available at JCSV III?
answer:
JCSV III provides shared village-wide facilities across its colleges, while each college also has its own specific amenities.

Village-wide facilities include student rooms with beds, wardrobes, writing desks, chairs, bookshelves and HKU Campus Network data ports; communal pantries on each floor with hot and cold water, induction cookers, microwave ovens, refrigerators and televisions; communal washrooms and shower stalls; laundry rooms operated by pre-paid smartcards; and shared WiFi (“HKU” and “WiFi.HK via HKU”) plus wired LAN ports in rooms [3][4][5]. The College Hall is a shared facility for communal events such as High Tables [2][5].

College-specific facilities vary by college. For example, Shun Hing College has 304 single and 85 double rooms, a music room (A-301), multifunctional spaces (A-303A, A-303B, A-303C, A-402), a 4/F Lobby with AV system, and laundry on 29/F [1][2][4]. For details of individual college amenities, please refer to each college’s own website [2].

Cleanliness and Conduct
• Remove all personal belongings and trash before leaving.

• Maintain a quiet environment and respect others using the space, especially in the Multi-
function Zone.

• No alcohol.

Event and Security Considerations

scheduled or ad hoc activities.

security checks. Please ensure you always have your student identification readily
available.

question: What should I do if I am locked out?
answer: If you are locked out, you may borrow your room key for door opening at the security counter of your College [1]. An administration fee of HK$20 will be charged each time the key is borrowed [1].

sources.title: Warm Reminder for Residents
sources.text:
Greetings from Jockey Club Student Village III! We would like to provide with you some warm reminders upon your move-in. Please read carefully.

Please make sure you have your room key and smart card (for air-conditioning and laundry) on your hand. For the use of smart card for laundry, please refer to the user guide in the laundry rooms (29/F in Shun Hing College and Chi Sun College; 26/F in Lap-Chee College and New College). The user guide of air-conditioning is posted in the lift lobby of each College. You may add value (HK$10 or its multiples) to your Smart Card by using the Smart Card Add Value Machine located next to the printer outside the General Office. No changes will be available or returned by the machine. However, please note that the remaining balance of smart card are non-refundable in all circumstances, including return of cards upon check-out and loss and/or replacement of cards.

Please remember to bring along your room key with you whenever you leave your room. The room doors are locked when closed, and should be opened with a room key. You may borrow your room key for door opening at the security counter of your College if you forget to bring it. An administration fee of HK$20 will be charged each time the key is borrowed.

Please return the following forms to the security counter of your College

Student Personal Information Form

In order to eliminate false alarm, which will cause disturbance to other residents in Jockey Club Student Village III, please DO NOT do the followings:
Ignite candle and aroma
Use pest fumigator

sources.title: Shun Hing Exchange Scholarships 25-26
sources.text:
Shun Hing Exchange Scholarships 2025-26
The
Shun Hing College Exchange Scholarship
is awarded to second or third-year undergraduate students who will be partaking in academic exchange for a year to universities in Japan under the HKU Worldwide Exchange Scheme or faculty-level exchange programmes.
Ma Cheuk Yin
-Exchange at University of Tokyo -
My name is Jiwoong Choi, a humble Korean student in the Bachelor of Arts program at the University of Hong Kong. Currently I’m spending my 3
rd
year as an exchange student at the University of Tokyo. Before I explain a bit more about my life in Japan, I would first like to express my deepest gratitude for having received the Shun Hing Scholarships for my exchange program. It’ll be of great help in pursuing countless opportunities during my time in Japan.
As an Arts student, my major is French but I also have an additional minor in the Japanese language. One of the most important factors in acquiring a language is how real of an experience can you gain during the process. To fully embrace a language, you must first understand the culture of the people that use it. The best way to do so is obviously living amongst them for a good amount of time, which is exactly what my exchange program in UTokyo is granting me of.
I’m looking forward to what I’ll come across during my stay in one of the grandest metropolises in the world, and I’ve no doubt that it’s going to be an enriching experience that I would treasure for a lifetime.
Lau Pak Kiu Ambrose
- Exchange at Rikkyo University-
